content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts show gradual upward drift (increasing trend) while true prices often exhibit sharp drops or mean-reversion after spikes.
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and continue rising, while true price often corrects downward or stabilizes.
- Model fails to capture sharp downward corrections in the middle of the 30d window; true prices often dip significantly after mid-period.
- Model underestimates late-period price volatility; true prices show stronger late-stage corrections or surges.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, especially when history includes recent high prices.
- Model does not adjust for mean reversion; forecasts remain elevated even when historical data shows downward momentum.
- Forecasts are overly smooth; true price movements often contain abrupt reversals or volatility clusters not captured by model.
